gloss: archive; museum; resource center; reference hall

definitions.gloss: archive; museum; resource center; reference hall
definitions.explanation: A facility that collects, preserves, and displays materials related to a specific topic, region, or historical period. Smaller and more specialized than a general museum.

examples.japanese: ⟦{郷土|きょうど}→郷土：14407_kyoudo⟧{資料館|しりょうかん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{訪|おとず}れた→訪れる：07678_otozureru⟧。
examples.english: I visited the local history archive.

examples.japanese: ⟦{歴史|れきし}→歴史：02267_rekishi⟧{資料館|しりょうかん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{古|ふる}い→古い：00488_furui⟧⟦{地図|ちず}→地図：02914_chizu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{展示|てんじ}→展示：12401_tenji⟧⟦されている→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Old maps are on display at the historical archive.

examples.japanese: ⟦{平和|へいわ}→平和：01507_heiwa⟧{資料館|しりょうかん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{戦争|せんそう}→戦争：01450_sensou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{悲惨|ひさん}→悲惨：12633_hisan⟧さ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{学|まな}んだ→学ぶ：01987_manabu⟧。
examples.english: I learned about the tragedy of war at the peace museum.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{資料|しりょう}→資料：04166_shiryou⟧ (materials, documents, data) + ⟦{館|かん}→館：17308_kan⟧ (hall, building). A common type of public institution in Japan, typically run by local governments.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{郷土|きょうど}→郷土：14407_kyoudo⟧{資料館|しりょうかん}: local history museum/archive
- ⟦{歴史|れきし}→歴史：02267_rekishi⟧{資料館|しりょうかん}: historical archive
- ⟦{平和|へいわ}→平和：01507_heiwa⟧{資料館|しりょうかん}: peace museum
- ⟦{民俗|みんぞく}→民俗：13238_minzoku⟧{資料館|しりょうかん}: folk culture museum

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{博物館|はくぶつかん}→博物館：01494_hakubutsukan⟧: museum — larger, more general institution with varied collections
- ⟦{図書館|としょかん}→図書館：00580_toshokan⟧: library — focused on books and lending; {資料館|しりょうかん} focuses on archival materials and exhibits
- {記念館|きねんかん}: memorial hall — dedicated to a specific person or event
- ⟦{美術館|びじゅつかん}→美術館：01717_bijutsukan⟧: art museum — specifically for fine art collections

USAGE:
Nearly every municipality in Japan has some form of {資料館|しりょうかん}. They are typically free or inexpensive to enter and serve an educational purpose. The word is often preceded by a modifier indicating the subject area.
